upstream.readme_sentence: The current catalogue contains 719 manuscripts organized into 372 families.

families.title: Milne’s rationality conjecture and algebraic specialization
families.upstream_summary: Proves Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties over ℚ with good reduction: specialized Hodge classes pair rationally with complementary divisor products, independently of cohomology theory. Together with result 032, every specialized Hodge class is represented by a single rational algebraic cycle simultaneously in all prime-to-p and crystalline realizations, for every residue characteristic p.

manuscripts.title: Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties

families.title: The full BSD formula from low Selmer corank
families.upstream_summary: Proves the full Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer leading-term formula for every elliptic curve over ℚ whose full q-power Selmer group has corank zero or one for some prime q, including finiteness of the Tate–Shafarevich group. With result 006, this gives full BSD for a density-one set of quadratic twists of every elliptic curve over ℚ.

manuscripts.title: The two-primary Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula in Selmer corank at most one
Exact Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Formula from Low Selmer Corank
The Selmer converse for elliptic curves at every prime

families.caution: BSD for low Selmer corank — not full BSD.

families.title: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis
families.upstream_summary: Proves that every Dirichlet L-function, including ζ(s), is zero-free in Re s > 7/8, resolving the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. The same half-plane is zero-free for every finite-order Hecke L-function over ℚ(√(-3)). A companion gives a different proof of the zero-free half-plane Re s > 11/12.

manuscripts.title: The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane Re s > 7/8
Uniform exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros
The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis (alternate 11/12 proof)

families.caution: Zero-free region Re s > 7/8 ('quasi-Riemann hypothesis') — not the Riemann Hypothesis.

families.title: Hilbert’s tenth problem over ℚ
families.upstream_summary: Proves that no algorithm decides whether an integer-coefficient polynomial in an arbitrary number of variables has a rational zero, resolving Hilbert's tenth problem over ℚ negatively.

manuscripts.title: Hilbert’s tenth problem over the rational numbers
A pointwise 2-converse for elliptic curves with rational two-torsion

families.title: Irrationality of Catalan’s constant
families.upstream_summary: Proves that Catalan's constant G=Σ_j ≥ 0(-1)^j/(2j+1)^2 is irrational.

manuscripts.title: Catalan's constant is irrational

families.title: Goldfeld’s conjecture: densities and mean analytic rank
families.upstream_summary: Proves Goldfeld's conjecture for quadratic twists of every elliptic curve over ℚ: analytic ranks zero and one each have density 1/2, and the mean analytic rank tends to 1/2. Both statements order signed squarefree twist parameters by absolute value.

manuscripts.title: The mean analytic rank of quadratic twists of elliptic curves
Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves

families.title: Ordinary two-point correlations and the corrected Elliott conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Proves the ordinary two-point Chowla conjecture, with a bound O(X/(log X)^c) for Liouville correlation sums along fixed nonproportional affine forms, where c > 0 is absolute. More generally, proves the binary corrected Elliott conjecture for complex multiplicative functions bounded by one when one factor is uniformly nonpretentious against each fixed Dirichlet character times n^it for |t| ≤ X.

manuscripts.title: Ordinary two-point correlations of multiplicative functions

reasoning_trace.subject: Ordinary two-point correlations of multiplicative functions

families.title: The Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Proves that the rational Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra, with the Ihara bracket, is freely generated by one element in each odd weight 3, 5, 7, …, resolving the Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture.

manuscripts.title: The Deligne-Drinfeld conjecture

families.title: Function-field reconstruction from Milnor K-theory and Galois data
families.upstream_summary: Reconstructs function fields of transcendence degree at least two over algebraically closed constants from K^M_1/ℓ, K^M_2/ℓ, and their product. These data recover the perfect closure and constants when ℓ differs from the characteristic, and the original field and its named base in equal characteristic. Also proves Bogomolov–Pop reconstruction from abelian-by-central pro-ℓ Galois data away from the characteristic.

manuscripts.title: The Bogomolov-Pop reconstruction theorem
Reconstruction from Milnor K-theory modulo the characteristic
Reconstruction of Function Fields from Mod-ℓ Milnor K-Theory

families.title: Unrestricted pro-modularity at the prime two
families.upstream_summary: Every continuous odd absolutely irreducible two-dimensional 2-adic representation of G_ℚ unramified outside finitely many primes occurs in a completed Hecke algebra at some odd tame level. Also proves classical modularity up to Tate twist for irreducible odd representations with these finiteness conditions that are de Rham at 2 with distinct Hodge–Tate weights, resolving the dyadic Fontaine–Mazur case without residual restrictions.

manuscripts.title: The Dimension of the Two-Adic Hecke Algebra at Odd Level
Fontaine–Mazur modularity at the prime 2
Unrestricted pro-modularity at the prime two

families.title: Prime-factor statistics of p-1
families.upstream_summary: Proves that the normalized ordered logarithms of the prime factors of p-1, counted with multiplicity, converge jointly to the Poisson–Dirichlet law PD(1) as p ranges uniformly over primes up to x and x → ∞. This resolves the Ford–Konyagin–Luca conjecture. It also proves that infinitely many integers n have more than n^1-ε totient preimages, for every ε > 0.

manuscripts.title: Prime Predecessors with an Even Number of Prime Factors
The Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors
Weighted dilation graphs, smooth shifted primes and totient fibers

families.title: Independent largest prime factors of consecutive integers
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the Erdős–Pomerance joint Dickman conjecture: the logarithmic sizes of the largest prime factors of n and n+1 are asymptotically independent in ordinary natural density. In particular, the integers satisfying P^+(n) < P^+(n+1) have density 1/2.

manuscripts.title: The joint Dickman law for consecutive integers

families.title: Ostmann’s inverse Goldbach conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Proves that no finite modification of the primes can be written as A+B with A,Bsubseteqℤ_ ≥ 0 each containing at least two elements. This resolves Ostmann's inverse Goldbach conjecture on additive indecomposability.

manuscripts.title: The additive indecomposability of the primes

families.title: Restricted geometric Langlands, global Arthur enhancements, and generic Ramanujan
families.upstream_summary: Proves the restricted geometric Langlands equivalence for connected reductive groups on smooth projective connected curves over 𝔽_q under the four stated Lie-theoretic characteristic hypotheses. Over arbitrary algebraically closed fields of characteristic p > 0, the same conclusion holds assuming additionally that p is very good for the group and pnmid |W_G|. Over global function fields, proves Ramanujan at every place for globally generic cuspidal representations of split adjoint absolutely simple exceptional groups, without characteristic or ramification-depth restrictions, and at every unramified place for cuspidal representations of split adjoint absolutely simple groups with a generic unramified component. Assuming the finite-level Ramanujan–Arthur decomposition, constructs global Arthur enhancements of occurring cuspidal excursion parameters for split connected semisimple groups at full finite level, recovering the given parameters by diagonal specialization on the entire Weil group, including inertia.

manuscripts.title: Ramanujan-Arthur Decompositions of Cuspidal Functions at Full Finite Level
Rationality of the Canonical Unramified Arthur Filtration
The Restricted Geometric Langlands Equivalence in Positive Characteristic
Constructible tame Hecke eigensheaves in positive characteristic
Frobenius Structures on Tame Hecke Eigensheaves
Global Arthur Enhancements of Cuspidal Excursion Parameters
Tame Hecke Eigensheaves with Several Marked Points
Temperedness at ramified places for globally generic exceptional groups

families.title: Torus-packet equidistribution in prime, quartic, and sextic degrees
families.upstream_summary: Proves Haar equidistribution without escape of mass for complete volume-weighted torus packets from totally real fields: arbitrary lattices and prescribed local types in fixed prime degree at least five, arbitrary-order Picard packets in primitive quartic fields, and maximal-order ideal-class packets in primitive sextic fields. Here primitive means having no proper intermediate field; the relevant order or field discriminant tends to infinity.

manuscripts.title: Equidistribution of Prime-Degree Torus Packets with Arbitrary Local Type
Equidistribution of primitive quartic torus packets for arbitrary orders
Equidistribution of Primitive Sextic Torus Packets

families.title: Zilber–Pink in abelian varieties and the Siegel threefold
families.upstream_summary: Proves the abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture over ℚ: every irreducible subvariety has finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties relative to its smallest containing torsion coset. It also proves the full curve case in the Siegel threefold A_2 for Hodge-generic curves defined over ℚ, without boundary or reduction assumptions.

manuscripts.title: Elliptic squares and Zilber–Pink for curves in A2
Quaternionic division points on curves in the Siegel threefold
The abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture
The E×CM component of Zilber–Pink for curves in A2

families.title: The irrationality exponent of π is 2
families.upstream_summary: Proves that the irrationality exponent of π is exactly 2: for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large denominators q, every rational p/q satisfies |π-p/q| ≥ q^-2-ε. This also proves convergence of the Flint–Hills series Σ_n ≥ 11/(n^3sin^2 n), with angles in radians.

manuscripts.title: The irrationality exponent of pi is 2

families.title: The Margulis–Platonov conjecture over global fields
families.upstream_summary: Proves the Margulis–Platonov conjecture over every global field, including function fields of characteristic two. For an absolutely almost simple simply connected algebraic group G over k, every noncentral abstract normal subgroup of G(k) is the inverse image of an open normal subgroup in the finite product of its anisotropic nonarchimedean local groups.

manuscripts.title: The Margulis–Platonov conjecture over number fields
The Margulis–Platonov conjecture over global function fields

families.title: The local p-adic section conjecture and global consequences
families.upstream_summary: Proves that rational points on every smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least two over a finite extension of ℚp correspond bijectively to conjugacy classes of sections of its full arithmetic étale fundamental group. It also proves Grothendieck's section conjecture over ℚ for the modular curves X_0(N) and X_1(N) of genus at least two.

manuscripts.title: Étale covers with a prescribed exterior sheet
The p-adic section conjecture

families.title: Squarefree quartics and power-free polynomial values
families.upstream_summary: Proves the squarefree-values conjecture for irreducible integer quartics with no fixed prime-square divisor: squarefree values on positive integers have the predicted positive Euler-product density. More generally, establishes the (d-2)-power-free density for irreducible integer polynomials of degrees four through eight under the necessary local condition; together with Browning's higher-degree theorem, this covers every d ≥ 4.

manuscripts.title: Squarefree values of quartics and power-free values of polynomials

families.title: A quadratic bound for Jacobsthal’s function
families.upstream_summary: Answers Jacobsthal's quadratic-bound question: every interval of Ck^2 consecutive integers contains an integer coprime to any prescribed positive integer with at most k distinct prime divisors, for an absolute constant C. The bound is uniform over prime sets and interval positions and removes the classical logarithmic loss.

manuscripts.title: A quadratic bound for Jacobsthal's function

families.title: The weak inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Proves that for every real shift γ and finite-valued ψ:ℕ → [0,∞), divergence of Σ_qφ(q)ψ(q)/q implies ‖qx-γ‖ < ψ(q) for infinitely many q, for almost every x. Here ϕ is Euler's totient and the norm is distance to the nearest integer. Numerators are unrestricted; no monotonicity or Diophantine condition on γ is needed.

manuscripts.title: The Weak Inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer Conjecture

families.title: Patterson's first moment for cubic Gauss sums
families.upstream_summary: Proves unconditionally the all-primary-prime form of Patterson’s first-moment asymptotic: normalized cubic Gauss sums over primary Eisenstein primes of norm at most X, including both conjugates, have an explicit positive main term of order X^5/6/log X. Every fixed nonzero prime-angle Fourier mode has smaller order.

manuscripts.title: An unconditional first moment for cubic Gauss sums

families.title: An asymptotic formula for the number of totients
families.upstream_summary: Gives an asymptotic equivalent for the number V(x) of distinct totient values up to x, with a positive bounded phase-dependent factor determined by convergent arithmetic approximations. In particular, V(cx)/V(x) → c for every fixed c > 0, answering Erdős and Hall’s scaling question.

manuscripts.title: An asymptotic formula for the number of totients

families.title: Short Egyptian fractions
families.upstream_summary: Every rational a/b with 1 ≤ a < b is a sum of O(loglog b) distinct positive unit fractions. The worst-case minimum number of terms has the same order, resolving Erdős’s conjecture on short Egyptian fractions.

manuscripts.title: Short Egyptian fractions

families.title: Positive lower density of large prime gaps
families.upstream_summary: For every fixed C > 0, a positive proportion of consecutive prime gaps exceed Clog p_n, throughout every sufficiently large initial segment of the primes. The proportion may depend on C. Consequently, the indices where p_n/n increases have positive lower density, answering Erdős and Prachar.

manuscripts.title: Positive lower density of large prime gaps

families.title: Potential integral density on curve character varieties
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the determinant-one curve case of Litt's integral-density question. For every smooth connected complex algebraic curve and every rank, integral points become Zariski dense in every component of its SLr character variety over the full ring of integers of one number field. Prescribed quasi-unipotent boundary conjugacy classes are allowed, including nonsemisimple classes.

manuscripts.title: Integral points on character varieties of curves

families.title: Uniformly bounded components of Gaussian-prime graphs
families.upstream_summary: Proves the Gaussian moat conjecture: no infinite walk through distinct Gaussian primes can have uniformly bounded steps. More strongly, for every distance bound D, the graph joining Gaussian primes at distance at most D has uniformly bounded finite component sizes, depending only on D, including primes on the coordinate axes.

manuscripts.title: Bounded-Step Walks on Gaussian Primes

families.title: Primitive roots for every admissible integer base
families.upstream_summary: Proves the infinitude assertion in Artin's primitive root conjecture for every integer a that is neither −1 nor a square. For each such base, at least c_a x/(log x)^2 primes in every sufficiently large interval (x,2x) have primitive root a, with c_a > 0.

manuscripts.title: Primitive roots for every admissible integer base
Simultaneous primitive roots: a conditional lower bound for prime bases

families.title: Modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields
families.upstream_summary: Proves the modularity conjecture for elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields: every elliptic curve over every imaginary quadratic field is modular, with matching local parameters at every place.

manuscripts.title: Modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields

families.title: Uchida’s conjecture for open homomorphisms of Galois groups
families.upstream_summary: Proves Uchida's conjecture: every continuous open homomorphism between Galois groups of possibly infinite solvably closed Galois extensions of number fields comes from a unique equivariant field embedding in the opposite direction. No restriction on the kernel or separate cyclotomic-compatibility assumption is needed.

manuscripts.title: Open Homomorphisms of Global Solvably Closed Galois Groups

families.title: The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties
families.upstream_summary: Proves the rational Hodge conjecture for every complex CM abelian variety, in every dimension and codimension. Through Milne's theorems, this also gives the Tate conjecture for all abelian varieties over finite fields and the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in every characteristic.

Abelian covers, Gale correspondences, and the Hodge conjecture for powers
The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties
Weil classes and Hodge classes on abelian powers

families.title: Iitaka subadditivity, variation, and logarithmic additivity
families.upstream_summary: Proves Campana's orbifold Iitaka subadditivity conjecture for smooth Fujiki-class-C manifolds with rational simple-normal-crossing boundaries. For projective fibrations f:U → V of smooth complex quasi-projective varieties with connected fibers, general fiber F, and barκ(V) ≥ 0, proves Popa's inequality barκ(U) ≥ κ(F)+maxbarκ(V),mathopVar (f), where variation measures the whole geometric generic fiber.

Logarithmic Kodaira dimension and whole-fiber variation
Orbifold and logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity
The reverse logarithmic Kodaira inequality and additivity
Projective Hodge lines and ordinary Iitaka subadditivity

families.title: Log abundance for compact Kähler spaces under logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity
families.upstream_summary: Using logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity, proves log abundance in every dimension for normal compact Kähler log canonical pairs with effective rational boundary: an analytically nef ℚ-Cartier adjoint is semiample. It also proves projective log abundance over every algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and the effective Iitaka fibration conjecture for smooth projective varieties of nonnegative Kodaira dimension in that setting. A further result resolves the finite-rational-coefficient index conjecture for connected projective semi-log-canonical log Calabi–Yau pairs over such fields in each fixed dimension and for each fixed finite set of rational boundary coefficients, with a uniform index independent of the number of components.

families.title: Log-canonical threefold abundance in numerical dimension one
families.upstream_summary: Proves log abundance for projective log canonical threefold pairs over algebraically closed fields of characteristic p > 3 when the effective boundary is rational and the ℚ-Cartier adjoint is nef of numerical dimension one. The adjoint is semiample, without requiring the original variety to be terminal or ℚ-factorial.

manuscripts.title: Abundance in numerical dimension one for terminal threefolds in positive characteristic
Log abundance in numerical dimension one for threefolds in positive characteristic

families.title: Numerical semiampleness and generalized minimal models
families.upstream_summary: Proves numerical semiampleness for nef adjoints K_X+B+M with K_X+B pseudo-effective and M nef rational, for projective klt rational pairs over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields and smooth compact Kähler rational klt simple-normal-crossing pairs, using Bott–Chern cohomology in the latter case. Separately, projective generalized log canonical rational pairs over such fields admit minimal models for pseudo-effective adjoints and Mori fiber spaces otherwise, with nef b-data fixed.

Minimal models in numerical dimension one
Numerical Semiampleness of Nef Adjoint Divisors
Numerical semiampleness of nef adjoint classes on compact Kähler manifolds

families.title: The ordinary-double-point volume gap
families.upstream_summary: Proves the ordinary-double-point volume-gap conjecture: every singular complex algebraic klt germ of dimension n ≥ 2, with zero boundary, has normalized volume at most 2(n-1)^n. Equality holds precisely for an analytic ordinary double point.

manuscripts.title: The normalized-volume gap in dimension four
The ordinary-double-point gap in every dimension

families.title: Fujita’s freeness conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Proves Fujita's freeness conjecture at its sharp bound in every dimension: for a smooth projective complex variety X of dimension n and an ample line bundle L, the adjoint K_X+mL is globally generated for every integer m ≥ n+1.

manuscripts.title: Fujita's freeness conjecture

families.title: Nagata’s conjecture and maximal Seshadri constants
families.upstream_summary: Proves Nagata's strict inequality Σ_i m_i < d√r for every nonzero effective plane curve of degree d through r ≥ 10 very general complex points, with arbitrary multiplicities mi. It also proves maximal multipoint Seshadri constants (L^n/r)^1/n for every smooth polarized projective variety of dimension n ≥ 2 and all sufficiently large r: at very general points over ℂ, and at the geometric generic tuple over any algebraically closed field of positive characteristic.

manuscripts.title: Maximal Seshadri constants on arbitrary polarized surfaces
Nagata's conjecture for plane curves
Maximal Multipoint Seshadri Constants in Higher Dimensions
Maximal multipoint Seshadri constants in positive characteristic

families.title: Bloch’s conjecture for complex surfaces
families.upstream_summary: Proves Bloch's conjecture: for every smooth connected projective complex surface S with p_g(S)=0, the Albanese map CH_0(S)^0 → Alb(S)(ℂ) on integral degree-zero zero-cycles is an isomorphism. This combines the new p_g=q=0 theorem with the classical theorem of Bloch, Kas, and Lieberman.

manuscripts.title: Bloch’s conjecture for surfaces with p_g=0

families.title: Hyperkähler SYZ and projective-space bases
families.upstream_summary: Proves the strong hyperkähler SYZ conjecture: every holomorphic line bundle with nonzero nef isotropic first Chern class on a compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic Kähler manifold is semiample. It also proves that every projective Lagrangian fibration with normal projective base has projective space as its base, in every dimension and deformation type.

manuscripts.title: Projective-space bases of Lagrangian fibrations
The strong hyperkähler SYZ conjecture

families.title: Oka classification for minimal compact complex surfaces: Kodaira dimension zero and class VII
families.upstream_summary: Proves that every complex K3 surface is Oka, including nonprojective surfaces. More generally, every connected minimal compact complex surface of Kodaira dimension zero is Oka; a connected minimal compact complex surface of class VII is Oka exactly when it is a Hopf or Enoki surface.

manuscripts.title: Every complex K3 surface is Oka

families.title: P = W for fixed-determinant SLₙ moduli spaces
families.upstream_summary: Proves P_k=W_2k=W_2k+1 on the full rational cohomology of smooth coprime fixed-determinant, trace-free Higgs moduli spaces and their character varieties for composite ranks over smooth projective complex curves of genus at least two. This includes variant cohomology and, together with the known prime-rank theorems, establishes the fixed-determinant P = W conjecture in every coprime rank.

manuscripts.title: P=W in composite rank for fixed determinant

families.title: The equivariant cohomological Hikita conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Proves the equivariant cohomological Hikita correspondence for every finite quiver, including loops and multiple arrows, with arbitrary dimension and framing vectors and commuting flavor torus. When every semistable point is stable and the gauge action is free, the equivariant cohomology of the Nakajima variety is canonically the coordinate ring of the scheme-theoretic cocharacter-fixed locus of its flavor-deformed Coulomb branch.

manuscripts.title: The equivariant cohomological Hikita conjecture for arbitrary quivers

families.title: Shafarevich counterexamples in dimension two and with large fundamental group
families.upstream_summary: Constructs a smooth projective complex fourfold with large fundamental group whose universal cover contains no positive-dimensional compact analytic subvariety but is neither Stein nor holomorphically convex. A separate smooth projective complex surface already disproves unrestricted Shafarevich holomorphic convexity in dimension two.

manuscripts.title: A surface counterexample to Shafarevich holomorphic convexity
A projective fourfold with large fundamental group and non-Stein universal cover

families.title: Zariski cancellation and affine fibrations over the complex numbers
families.upstream_summary: Constructs an integral complex affine fourfold XnotcongA^4 with X × A^1congA^5, disproving affine-space cancellation over ℂ in dimension four. It also disproves the Dolgachev–Weisfeiler affine-fibration conjecture: smooth surjections X → A^1 and A^5 → A^2 have every residue-field fiber isomorphic to affine three-space but are not Zariski-locally trivial.

manuscripts.title: An explicit failure of complex affine-space cancellation

families.title: A characteristic-zero counterexample to Lipman–Zariski
families.upstream_summary: Constructs a singular normal affine complex surface with free rank-two tangent sheaf, disproving the characteristic-zero Lipman–Zariski conjecture.

manuscripts.title: A singular normal affine surface with free tangent sheaf

families.title: A stable-coordinate counterexample in four variables
families.upstream_summary: Constructs a polynomial in four complex variables that is not a coordinate but becomes one after adjoining a single variable, disproving the Stable Coordinate conjecture in four variables. Every fiber is affine three-space, yet none of its embeddings is rectifiable, also disproving the Abhyankar–Sathaye conjecture even when all fibers are affine spaces.

manuscripts.title: An explicit noncoordinate polynomial with affine three-space zero fibre
A stable coordinate that is not a coordinate in four variables

families.title: A counterexample to Griffiths’ positivity conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Constructs ample rank-two bundles on P^1 × P^1 with no smooth Hermitian metric of strictly Griffiths-positive curvature, disproving Griffiths' positivity conjecture already on the quadric surface.

manuscripts.title: Ample rank-two bundles on the quadric surface without Griffiths-positive metrics

families.title: Kobayashi’s canonical-ampleness conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Every compact connected Kähler manifold of positive complex dimension with no nonconstant entire curve has ample canonical bundle and is therefore projective. This proves Kobayashi's canonical-ampleness conjecture in the smooth compact Kähler setting.

manuscripts.title: Canonical ampleness of compact hyperbolic Kähler manifolds

families.title: Tangent splittings and product decompositions
families.upstream_summary: A splitting of the tangent bundle of a compact Kähler manifold into two integrable holomorphic subbundles induces a compatible product decomposition of its universal cover, proving the two-summand form of Beauville's splitting conjecture. On smooth rationally connected projective manifolds, both summands are automatically integrable, establishing Höring's conjecture and the corresponding product decomposition.

manuscripts.title: Integrability of split tangent bundles on rationally connected manifolds
Universal-cover splitting for compact Kähler manifolds

families.title: A counterexample to Pixton completeness in Chow
families.upstream_summary: Constructs a tautological relation on a moduli space of stable pointed curves that vanishes in rational Chow, hence in rational cohomology, but lies outside Pixton's original relation span. This disproves the Chow and rational-cohomological forms of his original completeness conjecture.

manuscripts.title: A high-arity counterexample to Pixton completeness in Chow

families.title: Irrational cubic fourfolds with Hodge-theoretic and categorical K3 associations
families.upstream_summary: For every sufficiently large admissible Hassett discriminant, a very general smooth complex cubic fourfold is irrational despite having both an untwisted geometric K3 category and an integral Hodge-theoretic K3 association. This disproves Kuznetsov's rationality conjecture and the sufficiency of the associated-K3 criterion for rationality; the discriminant threshold is ineffective.

manuscripts.title: Irrational cubic fourfolds with geometric K3 categories

families.title: Gepner symmetry and large-volume stability on threefolds
families.upstream_summary: Proves Toda's Gepner conjecture for every smooth complex quintic threefold, constructing a numerical Bridgeland stability condition with the prescribed phase shift 2/5. Also constructs numerical Bridgeland stability conditions at every sufficiently large volume on all smooth projective complex threefolds with trivial canonical bundle, with the exact ordinary and square-root-Todd central charges.

manuscripts.title: A Gepner stability condition on every smooth quintic threefold
Prescribed large-volume charges on threefolds with trivial canonical bundle

families.title: Termination of projective and Kähler fourfold minimal model programs
families.upstream_summary: Proves termination of every existing generalized log canonical flip sequence on globally Weil ℚ-factorial compact Kähler fourfolds, with rational boundary, fixed rational analytically nef b-data, and projective small flip diagrams with the prescribed ample signs. Also proves termination of arbitrary permitted minimal model programs for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary in characteristic zero.

manuscripts.title: Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds
Termination for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary
Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds
Termination of generalized-canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds
Termination of generalized log canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds

families.title: Fundamental groups of special complex varieties and root orbifolds
families.upstream_summary: Proves Campana's abelianity conjecture: special compact Kähler manifolds have virtually abelian fundamental groups. Using this theorem, establishes the same conclusion for order-two root orbifolds of smooth projective complex fourfolds along one nonempty smooth connected divisor, when special in the stated differential-line sense. For smooth special complex quasi-projective varieties, proves that every finite-dimensional complex linear representation of the fundamental group has virtually nilpotent image of class at most two.

manuscripts.title: The abelianity conjecture for special compact Kähler manifolds
Two-step monodromy of special quasi-projective varieties
A conditional abelianity theorem for special fourfold pairs with a half-weight divisor

families.title: Semialgebraic universal covers and bounded domains
families.upstream_summary: Proves the Kollár–Pardon conjecture: the semialgebraic universal covers of connected normal projective complex varieties are exactly products D × ℂ^m × F, with D bounded symmetric and F simply connected, normal, and projective. A universal cover is quasi-projective exactly when the bounded symmetric factor is absent. In particular, a smooth projective variety covered by ℂⁿ has a finite étale cover by an abelian variety.

manuscripts.title: Semialgebraic universal covers of normal projective varieties
Symmetry of semialgebraic bounded domains with compact quotient

families.title: Counterexamples to Zariski’s multiplicity conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Disproves Zariski's multiplicity conjecture by constructing reduced holomorphic hypersurface germs that are ambiently homeomorphic but have different multiplicities. The examples include hypersurfaces in ℂ⁴ with isolated critical points and multiplicities four and five.

manuscripts.title: Ambiently homeomorphic isolated hypersurfaces of multiplicities two and three
Ambiently homeomorphic isolated hypersurface germs in ℂ⁴ with multiplicities four and five

families.title: The Global Spherical Shell conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Every connected minimal compact complex surface of class VII with b_2 > 0 contains a global spherical shell, proving the positive-b₂ Global Spherical Shell conjecture. Such a shell is a holomorphically embedded neighborhood of the standard three-sphere in ℂ^2setminus0 whose complement is connected.

A uniform decoder achieves quasipolynomial sample and running-time bounds for known fixed rational retention probabilities. When the deletion probability is at most n^-ε for fixed ε > 0, both bounds become polynomial in the input and parameter encoding.

manuscripts.title: Quantitative lower bounds for trace reconstruction
A latest-anchor induction with spectrally compact masks for worst-case trace reconstruction
Uniform quasipolynomial-time trace reconstruction

families.title: Polynomial-time scheduling on three identical machines
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the three-processor unit-job scheduling problem of Garey and Johnson: a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm minimizes makespan for nonpreemptive unit-length jobs with arbitrary precedence constraints on three identical parallel machines. For an explicitly given precedence graph, it decides deadline feasibility exactly and constructs a feasible schedule.

manuscripts.title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Three-Machine Unit-Job Scheduling

families.title: The metric k-median approximation threshold and recovery
families.upstream_summary: Gives a deterministic polynomial-time (1+2/e+ε)-approximation for finite rational metric k-median with specified candidate facilities, for every fixed ε > 0. Assuming Pne NP, the optimal infimum approximation factor is 1+2/e.

manuscripts.title: Single-exponential recovery and bounded-price strictness for metric k-median
The approximation threshold for metric k-median

families.title: Exponential semidefinite complexity of perfect matching
families.upstream_summary: Proves that every exact semidefinite lift of the perfect matching polytope has exponential size, answering Rothvoss's polynomial-size lift question negatively. The bound holds even for the positive semidefinite rank of its odd-cut slack matrix after any fixed shift 0 < ρ < 1, allowing arbitrary real positive semidefinite factors.

manuscripts.title: Exponential PSD rank of positively shifted matching matrices

lenses.why: The family treats semidefinite extension complexity of the perfect matching polytope.

families.title: Average sensitivity of polynomial threshold functions
families.upstream_summary: Proves that a degree-at-most-d polynomial threshold function on the uniform n-dimensional Boolean cube has average sensitivity at most 8d√n, uniformly for 1 ≤ d ≤ n. Average sensitivity counts expected output changes under single-bit flips. This establishes the asymptotic Gotsman–Linial conjecture, allowing polynomial zeros with mathopsign (0)=1.

manuscripts.title: Average sensitivity of polynomial threshold functions

families.title: A factor-two approximation for shortest common superstring
families.upstream_summary: Gives a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm constructing a common superstring of length at most twice the optimum for every finite family of explicitly represented strings. The running time is polynomial in the full encoded input length, including symbol labels.

manuscripts.title: A Polynomial-Time 2-Approximation for Shortest Common Superstring

families.title: Exponential state costs for two-way automata
families.upstream_summary: Proves exponential lower bounds both for complementing two-way nondeterministic finite automata and for simulating one-way nondeterministic automata by two-way deterministic ones. The latter resolves the Sakoda–Sipser state-succinctness conjecture over growing finite alphabets; both results rule out polynomial state bounds independent of alphabet size.

manuscripts.title: An exponential state lower bound for two-way nondeterministic complementation
An exponential two-way deterministic state lower bound for one-way liveness

families.title: Exact Fourier transforms below nlog n
families.upstream_summary: Gives a deterministic length-n discrete Fourier transform algorithm using O(n(log n)^1-δ) operations for every n, with explicit δ=10^-13. The model uses exact complex arithmetic, unrestricted coefficients and a supplied root of unity, and counts scalar preparation and logarithmic-word indexing.

manuscripts.title: An explicit power saving for the exact discrete Fourier transform
Finite tensor savings and exact Fourier circuits

families.title: Rapid mixing of graph switches for every degree sequence
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the simple-undirected Kannan–Tetali–Vempala conjecture: the lazy edge-switch chain mixes in O(n^8) time for every graphical labeled degree sequence. The same degree-constrained graphs can also be sampled exactly uniformly by an almost-surely terminating algorithm with expected polynomial bit running time.

manuscripts.title: Polynomial mixing of the switch chain for every graphical degree sequence

families.title: A superquadratic separation of sensitivity and block sensitivity
families.upstream_summary: Constructs total Boolean functions with block sensitivity mathopbs (f) ≥ s(f)^α for a fixed α > 2, disproving the quadratic strengthening of the Sensitivity Conjecture. Here s(f) counts influential individual-bit flips, while block sensitivity allows disjoint groups of bits to change together.

manuscripts.title: A superquadratic separation between sensitivity and block sensitivity

families.title: The computational complexity of Weisfeiler–Leman refinement
families.upstream_summary: Proves unconditional n^Omega(k) deterministic time lower bounds for joint and separate k-dimensional Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence, for sufficiently large fixed k in the specified sequential adjacency-matrix models. With dimension as input, joint equivalence is EXPTIME-complete even on subcubic graphs; deciding whether refinement identifies a graph is also EXPTIME-complete.

manuscripts.title: Parity lifts and bounded-treewidth witnesses for Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence
The complexity of identifying a graph by Weisfeiler–Leman refinement
Unconditional time lower bounds for Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence
Variable-dimension Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence on general and subcubic graphs

families.title: Generalized star height at most three
families.upstream_summary: Every regular language over a finite alphabet has a generalized regular expression with at most three nested Kleene stars, allowing union, concatenation and complement over the same alphabet. This establishes an absolute bound independent of automaton size, resolving the uniform-boundedness version of the generalized star-height problem.

manuscripts.title: Finite Monoid Computations and a Uniform Generalized Star-Height Bound
Generalized Star Height at Most Four
Generalized Star Height at Most Three

families.title: Homogeneous depth-five lower bounds for iterated matrix multiplication
families.upstream_summary: Over every characteristic-zero field, the (1,1) entry of a product of n independent n × n variable matrices requires n^Theta(√n) gates in homogeneous depth-five sum–product circuits. This sharp bound allows shared gates and bottom linear forms involving all variables.

manuscripts.title: Homogeneous depth-five lower bounds for iterated matrix multiplication

families.title: A quasilinear PCP theorem for PPAD
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the quasilinear PCP-for-PPAD conjecture. An End-of-Line instance of length N reduces to numerical circuit constraints of total length N(log N)^O(1) such that any polynomially encoded rational assignment satisfying all but a fixed fraction to fixed accuracy yields an endpoint solution. Such assignments always exist, giving robust local verification with only quasilinear size overhead.

manuscripts.title: The PCP-for-PPAD conjecture: a quasilinear reduction

families.title: One-tape time simulation in two-fifths-power space
families.upstream_summary: Determines the halting and finite-control outcome of a fixed deterministic one-writable-tape machine up to time T using O(T^2/5log^C(T+2)) space, improving the square-root exponent. Heads move at most one cell per step; finitely many read-only input heads are allowed. Initial contents are independent of T, and contents and input symbols have polylogarithmic-space access. Simulation time is unrestricted.

manuscripts.title: Simulating One-Tape Time in Two-Fifths-Power Space

families.title: Subset Sum in O(2^0.49n) time
families.upstream_summary: Gives a uniform randomized classical algorithm for worst-case Subset Sum in ordinary O(2^0.49n) word-RAM time on polynomial-bit inputs, where n counts the integers. The time bound holds on every execution and success probability is at least 2/3 on every input. Inputs may repeat positive integers; words have O(n+b) bits for maximum input bit length b.

manuscripts.title: A Low-Space Algorithm for Worst-Case Subset Sum
Subset Sum in Time O(2^0.49n)

families.title: Subpolynomial query complexity for log-concave sampling
families.upstream_summary: For C² potentials with a supplied minimizer and Ipreceqnabla^2Vpreceq2I, proves that sampling within total variation 1/10 requires only C_ε d^ε exact value-and-gradient queries for every fixed ε > 0. The bound holds on every run, with unrestricted computation between queries. A logarithmic lower bound also holds, so the optimal power-law exponent in this oracle model is zero.

manuscripts.title: Subpolynomial query complexity for well-conditioned log-concave sampling

lenses.why: The family treats query complexity of sampling log-concave densities.

families.title: Memory–sample lower bounds for noiseless Gaussian regression
families.upstream_summary: For fixed A > 0, a one-pass learner with Ad^2 persistent bits needs Omega_A(dlog(1/ε)) noiseless Gaussian samples to recover a unit vector to angular error 0 < ε ≤ 1/10 with probability 2/3, uniformly in accuracy for large d. Computation and randomized updates are unrestricted, but output uses only the terminal state, stopping index and fresh randomness.

manuscripts.title: Localization costs and information growth for exact Gaussian observations
Memory and precision in noiseless Gaussian regression
Posterior replicas and conditional information in Gaussian regression
Projection moments, positive cap domination, and Riesz estimates on the sphere
Replacing Gaussian observations in memory-constrained inference
Subsphere methods for memory-sample lower bounds in noiseless Gaussian regression

families.title: Existential–universal real sentences in the counting hierarchy
families.upstream_summary: Proves that the existential theory of the reals lies in the counting hierarchy. More generally, truth of existential–universal real sentences can be decided at one fixed level of that hierarchy, even when their integer polynomials are specified by arithmetic circuits.

manuscripts.title: Existential–universal real sentences in the counting hierarchy

families.title: Deterministic polynomial factorization over prime fields
families.upstream_summary: Gives a uniform deterministic algorithm that completely factors every nonzero dense degree-n polynomial over a prime field 𝔽p, including multiplicities, in bit complexity polynomial in (n+1)log p. The prime is supplied in binary. No randomness, integer-factorization or primitive-root oracle, or GRH assumption is required.

manuscripts.title: Deterministic Polynomial Factorization over Prime Fields

families.title: Hilbert's sixteenth problem: uniform bounds for limit cycles
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the uniform boundedness assertion in Hilbert's sixteenth problem: the number of isolated periodic orbits of a real planar polynomial vector field is bounded by a finite constant depending only on its degree. For classical quintic Liénard systems, the exact maximum is two limit cycles.

manuscripts.title: Two limit cycles for quintic Liénard systems
Uniform bounds for planar polynomial limit cycles

families.title: Banach’s simple Lebesgue-spectrum problem
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the probability-preserving form of Banach's simple Lebesgue-spectrum problem within smooth dynamics. A smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphism of the standard-volume three-torus has simple Lebesgue spectrum on its entire complex mean-zero L² space: the bilateral iterates of one real observable form an orthonormal basis of that space.

manuscripts.title: A smooth three-torus diffeomorphism with simple Lebesgue spectrum

families.title: Rokhlin’s multiple-mixing problem
families.upstream_summary: Proves that every invertible mixing probability-preserving transformation is mixing of all finite orders, resolving Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for a single transformation. Correlations among any finite collection of measurable sets converge to the product of their measures whenever all pairwise time separations diverge.

manuscripts.title: Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for one transformation

families.title: Positive metric entropy for the standard map
families.upstream_summary: Proves that the standard sine map on the two-dimensional torus has positive metric entropy with respect to area for every sufficiently large positive parameter. This establishes Sinai's positive-parameter-measure conjecture for the original family, with the stronger conclusion of a full parameter tail.

manuscripts.title: Positive Metric Entropy for the Standard Map at Large Parameters

families.title: The near-boundary Birkhoff conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the near-boundary Birkhoff conjecture for smooth strictly convex planar billiards of positive curvature. Such a billiard is an ellipse whenever a full grazing annulus is continuously foliated by individually invariant essential curves. A continuous physical collar of smooth closed convex caustics also suffices.

manuscripts.title: Continuous Phase Foliations Create Analytic Caustic Collars
Rigidity of Smooth Billiards with a Continuous Caustic Collar

families.title: The entropy-rate dimension formula for self-similar measures
families.upstream_summary: For every self-similar measure on the line generated by finitely many contracting similarities, proves dim_Hμ=min1,h_RW/chi, where h_RW is the entropy rate of random composed maps and χ the average logarithmic contraction. This resolves the entropy-rate dimension conjecture without a separation assumption, allowing exact overlaps and unequal contraction ratios.

manuscripts.title: The entropy-rate dimension formula for self-similar measures on the line

families.title: Classwise permanence for weakly reversible mass-action systems
families.upstream_summary: Proves the permanence conjecture for every finite weakly reversible mass-action system with fixed positive rate constants. Every positive stoichiometric compatibility class, even an unbounded one, has a common compact convex forward-invariant absorbing set. All positive trajectories in that class therefore eventually share positive lower and finite upper concentration bounds.

manuscripts.title: Boundedness and persistence of weakly reversible mass-action systems
Uniform Permanence in Weakly Reversible Mass-Action Systems

families.title: Weak mixing of triangular billiards with an irrational angle
families.upstream_summary: Proves that the billiard flow in every nondegenerate Euclidean triangle with at least one angle irrational relative to π is weakly mixing for normalized area times uniform direction. This strengthens ergodicity on the entire irrational-angle class, with no genericity or Diophantine restrictions.

manuscripts.title: Ergodicity of triangular billiards with an irrational angle
Weak mixing of triangular billiards with an irrational angle

families.title: A C¹ counterexample to the entropy conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Constructs a noninvertible C¹ self-map of a compact smooth manifold with zero topological entropy but eigenvalue 2 on second homology. This disproves the homological entropy lower bound for general C¹ self-maps: homological growth need not force positive orbit complexity.

manuscripts.title: A C^1 Counterexample to the Entropy Conjecture

families.title: Zero entropy does not guarantee a smooth positive-volume model
families.upstream_summary: Constructs a zero-entropy ergodic invertible transformation of a standard nonatomic probability space that is not measurably conjugate to any C∞ diffeomorphism preserving a strictly positive smooth probability density on a compact finite-dimensional manifold. One example rules out every finite dimension.

manuscripts.title: A zero-entropy system without a smooth positive-volume model

families.title: Arithmetic classification and non-Pisot singularity for Bernoulli convolutions
families.upstream_summary: Classifies singular and absolutely continuous unbiased Bernoulli convolutions for every λin(0,1) by an infinite, one-sided approximation condition using explicit finite sets of algebraic units. It also proves singularity at reciprocals of every quartic Salem number in (1,2), giving examples beyond reciprocal Pisot parameters.

manuscripts.title: Arithmetic classification and non-Pisot singularity for Bernoulli convolutions

families.title: Pointwise multiple ergodic averages for mixing transformations
families.upstream_summary: Proves almost-everywhere convergence of consecutive multiple ergodic averages of every finite length for invertible mixing probability-preserving transformations. For each fixed tuple of bounded functions, the limit is the product of their integrals, along all positive averaging lengths. No mixing rate or standardness assumption on the probability space is required.

manuscripts.title: Pointwise Multiple Ergodic Averages for Mixing Transformations
Pointwise convergence of fourfold ergodic averages for mixing transformations
Pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages for mixing transformations
Triple ergodic averages with distinct integer slopes

families.title: A counterexample to periodic tiling in dimension three
families.upstream_summary: Constructs a finite translational tile in ℤ³ that tiles space but admits no fully periodic tiling, disproving the periodic tiling conjecture in the smallest possible lattice dimension. Its unit-cube thickening gives the same counterexample in ℝ³, even with arbitrary real translation vectors.

manuscripts.title: A translational tile with no fully periodic tiling in dimension three

families.title: Borsuk's conjecture fails in dimension nine
families.upstream_summary: Constructs a compact subset of ℝ⁹ that cannot be covered by ten sets of strictly smaller diameter, disproving Borsuk's covering assertion already in dimension nine. The example consists of rank-one orthogonal projectors onto lines in ℝ⁴, with the Frobenius metric.

manuscripts.title: A nine-dimensional counterexample to Borsuk's covering assertion

families.title: Graph coloring, clique minors, and Colin de Verdière invariants
families.upstream_summary: Disproves Hadwiger's conjecture even for fractional coloring: arbitrarily large finite simple graphs with independence number at most two satisfy chi_f(G) > h(G), where h(G) is the largest clique-minor order. Also disproves the fractional Colin de Verdière chromatic bound chi_f(G) ≤ μ(G)+1. In the positive direction, every finite nonempty graph satisfies chi_list(G) ≤ C h(G) for a universal constant C.

manuscripts.title: A counterexample to Hadwiger's conjecture
A counterexample to the Colin de Verdière chromatic conjecture
A linear list-coloring bound in terms of the Hadwiger number

families.title: The Euclidean plane cannot be colored with five colors
families.upstream_summary: Proves that every five-coloring of the Euclidean plane has a monochromatic pair at distance one, with no restriction on the color classes. This advances the Hadwiger–Nelson problem: together with the classical seven-coloring, only six and seven remain possible chromatic numbers of the plane.

manuscripts.title: The Euclidean plane is not five-colorable

families.title: Erdős’s reciprocal-sum conjecture and quasipolynomial Szemerédi bounds
families.upstream_summary: Proves Erdős's conjecture that every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length. Quantitatively, for each fixed k ≥ 3, every subset of 1,ldots,N with no nonconstant k-term progression has size at most C_kNexp[-c_k(log N)^ε_k], with positive constants depending only on k.

manuscripts.title: Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions

families.title: Superexponential van der Waerden numbers
families.upstream_summary: Resolves Erdős's superexponential-growth question for van der Waerden numbers. If W_r(k) is the least interval length forcing a monochromatic k-term progression in every r-coloring, then W_r(k) > k^cklfloorlog_2 rrfloor for an absolute c > 0, all r ≥ 2 and sufficiently large k, uniformly in r. In particular, W_r(k)^1/k → ∞ for each fixed r.

manuscripts.title: Quantitative Superexponential Bounds for van der Waerden Numbers

families.title: Counterexamples to Sidorenko’s conjecture and the forcing conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Disproves Sidorenko's conjecture with a connected bipartite pattern on 35 vertices and 66 edges that occurs less frequently than in a random graph of the same edge density. The same pattern disproves the forcing conjecture of Skokan and Thoma: matching its density and the edge density of a constant graphon need not force quasirandomness.

manuscripts.title: A counterexample to Sidorenko's conjecture

families.title: Counterexamples to Ryser’s covering conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Disproves Ryser's covering conjecture by constructing intersecting (q+1)-partite, (q+1)-uniform hypergraphs with covering number q+1, rather than the predicted bound q, for every sufficiently large prime q. A separate construction over extension fields also disproves Gyárfás's monochromatic tree-cover conjecture.

manuscripts.title: A counterexample to Ryser's covering conjecture
Balanced counterexamples to Ryser's conjecture at prime orders

families.title: Hindman’s finite sums and products conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Proves Hindman's finite sums and products conjecture: every finite coloring of the positive integers contains sets of any prescribed finite size whose nonempty subset sums and nonempty subset products all have one common color.

manuscripts.title: Monochromatic finite sums and products in the positive integers

families.title: The Harary–Hill and Zarankiewicz crossing-number formulas
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the Harary–Hill conjecture and Turán's brickyard problem in the Zarankiewicz formulation, determining the crossing numbers of every complete and complete bipartite graph. The result proves the optimality of the classical drawings among all plane drawings with continuous edge arcs.

manuscripts.title: The crossing number of complete bipartite graphs
The crossing number of complete graphs

families.title: The higher-dimensional Erdős distinct-distances conjecture
families.upstream_summary: For every fixed d ≥ 3, any n ≥ 2 distinct points in ℝd determine at least c_dn^2/d distinct distances, with c_d > 0 depending only on dimension. This matches the integer-grid order and resolves the higher-dimensional Erdős distinct-distances conjecture with a constant-factor bound.

manuscripts.title: The higher-dimensional Erdős distinct-distances conjecture

families.title: Planar distinct distances and unit-distance bounds
families.upstream_summary: Proves the weak pinned Erdős distance conjecture: for every fixed ε > 0, all but o(n) points of any n-point planar set determine at least n^1-ε distinct nonzero distances. A complementary theorem bounds the number of unit-distance pairs by O(n^4/3-δ) for an absolute δ > 0.

manuscripts.title: A power saving for planar unit distances
The weak pinned planar distance theorem

families.title: Combinatorial invariance of Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the full combinatorial invariance conjecture: isomorphic Bruhat intervals in arbitrary Coxeter systems have identical equal-parameter Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials. Thus the abstract order of the interval determines the polynomial, even across different Coxeter systems.

manuscripts.title: Combinatorial invariance of Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials

families.title: Shareshian–Wachs elementary positivity
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the elementary-positivity part of the Shareshian–Wachs conjecture: the chromatic quasisymmetric function of every natural unit interval graph has elementary-basis coefficients in ℕ[q]. The coefficients count explicitly described permutations, giving a combinatorial explanation of positivity.

manuscripts.title: Elementary positivity of chromatic quasisymmetric functions

families.title: Sharp logarithmic exponents for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers
families.upstream_summary: For every fixed integer s ≥ 5, proves r(s,t)=t^s-1/(log t)^s-2+o(1) as t → ∞, determining the logarithmic exponent and matching the classical upper bound at that scale. Here r(s,t) is the least number of vertices forcing an s-clique or a t-vertex independent set.

manuscripts.title: Sharp logarithmic exponents for fixed off-diagonal Ramsey numbers
The sharp logarithmic exponent of r(5,t)

families.title: The hypercube Ramsey conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the Burr–Erdős hypercube Ramsey conjecture: the two-color Ramsey number of the n-dimensional cube is Theta(2^n). Thus every red-blue coloring of a complete graph on a universal constant times the cube's number of vertices contains a monochromatic copy of the cube.

manuscripts.title: The hypercube Ramsey number has linear order

families.title: Classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations
families.upstream_summary: Classifies finite point configurations that occur monochromatically, at their original scale, in every finite coloring of sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space. The characterization is an algebraic condition over the coordinate field. It also disproves the Leader–Russell–Walters conjecture that every such configuration is a subset of a finite transitive set.

manuscripts.title: A classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations

families.title: Seymour’s second-neighborhood conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Proves Seymour's second-neighborhood conjecture: every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex with at least as many vertices at directed distance exactly two as at directed distance one. Oriented graphs may be arbitrary apart from the exclusion of loops and oppositely directed edge pairs.

manuscripts.title: A proof of Seymour’s second-neighborhood conjecture

families.title: Deterministic construction of strong thin spanning trees
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the strong thin-tree conjecture constructively. Every finite loopless k-edge-connected multigraph on at least two vertices has a spanning tree containing at most a universal C/k fraction of the edges of every cut. Such a tree can be found deterministically in polynomial time, even with binary-encoded parallel-edge multiplicities.

manuscripts.title: A polynomial-time construction of strong thin trees
The strong thin tree conjecture

families.title: Talagrand’s expectation thresholds, discrete convexity, and graph decompositions
families.upstream_summary: Proves that integral and fractional expectation thresholds differ by at most a universal factor, and resolves Talagrand's discrete-convexity conjecture. An application proves the Ascoli–He–Park–Talagrand graph-decomposition conjecture: every graph's edges split into a universally bounded number of fixed pieces, each with containment threshold at most a universal constant times the original graph's integral expectation threshold. The pieces' embeddings need not agree on shared vertices.

manuscripts.title: Integral and fractional expectation thresholds are equivalent
Talagrand’s discrete-convexity conjecture
Graph Decompositions at the Integral Expectation Threshold

families.title: The second Kahn–Kalai conjecture with an edge-count bound
families.upstream_summary: Proves the second Kahn–Kalai conjecture: for every finite simple graph H with h ≥ 1 edges and at most n vertices, its appearance threshold in G(n,p) is at most C p_E(n,H)(1+log_2 h), with universal C. Here p_E is the least density at which every subgraph of H has expected copy count at least 1/2.

manuscripts.title: The second Kahn–Kalai conjecture

families.title: Bounded-degree coboundary expanders
families.upstream_summary: Constructs arbitrarily large finite d-dimensional simplicial complexes, for every d ≥ 3, with uniformly bounded vertex degrees and uniform 𝔽₂ coboundary expansion in every degree below d. Together with the known graph and two-dimensional cases, this establishes the existence of such expanders in every positive dimension.

manuscripts.title: Bounded-degree coboundary expanders in every dimension

families.title: Deterministic nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs in every fixed degree
families.upstream_summary: For every fixed d ≥ 3, constructs a simple d-regular nonbipartite Ramanujan graph on every sufficiently large even number n of vertices, with every nonconstant adjacency eigenvalue strictly between -2√(d-1) and 2√(d-1). A deterministic algorithm outputs the full adjacency list in polynomial bit time, with exponent depending on d.

manuscripts.title: Deterministic nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs in every fixed degree

families.title: The circulant Hadamard and Barker-sequence conjectures
families.upstream_summary: Proves that real circulant Hadamard matrices exist exactly in orders 1 and 4, resolving the circulant Hadamard conjecture. Together with classical Barker-sequence results, this shows that binary sequences whose nontrivial aperiodic autocorrelations have magnitude at most 1 exist at lengths n > 1 exactly when nin2,3,4,5,7,11,13.

manuscripts.title: The circulant Hadamard conjecture

families.title: Barnette’s Hamiltonian-cycle conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Proves that every finite simple cubic bipartite planar 3-vertex-connected graph has a Hamiltonian cycle, resolving Barnette's conjecture. Equivalently, every three-edge path in a finite simple cubic 3-vertex-connected bipartite Pfaffian graph lies in a Hamiltonian cycle.

manuscripts.title: Paired states and Hamiltonian cycles in cubic bipartite planar graphs

families.title: The Erdős–Gallai cycle-decomposition conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Proves that the edges of every finite simple undirected graph on n vertices can be partitioned into at most Cn simple cycles and single edges, for an absolute constant C. This resolves the Erdős–Gallai cycle-decomposition conjecture, bounding the number of pieces linearly even for dense graphs.

manuscripts.title: A linear cycle-and-edge decomposition of every graph

families.title: Power savings for intersective polynomial differences and prime arguments
families.upstream_summary: For every fixed intersective integer polynomial h of degree k ≥ 2 with positive leading coefficient, proves that a subset of 1,ldots,N avoiding nonzero values h(1),h(2),ldots as differences has size O_h(N^1-c_k), with c_k > 0 depending only on degree. Here intersective means having a root modulo every modulus. For prime arguments, a power saving also holds when h has a unit root modulo every modulus, with exponent allowed to depend on h.

manuscripts.title: A power saving for square-difference-free sets
A Power Saving for Polynomial Differences at Prime Arguments
A power saving for intersective polynomial differences with an exponent depending only on the degree

families.title: Power savings for planar halving lines and k-sets
families.upstream_summary: Improves the planar halving-line bound to O(n^4/3-ε) for sets with no three collinear and an absolute ε > 0. More generally, an n-point set with no three collinear has O(n(k+1)^1/3-ε_0) strictly separable k-subsets for 1 ≤ k ≤ n/2, with an absolute ε_0 > 0. The constants and positive exponents are nonquantitative.

manuscripts.title: A power saving for planar halving lines

families.title: Correspondence coloring with a fixed forbidden subgraph
families.upstream_summary: Proves the Alon–Krivelevich–Sudakov coloring conjecture in correspondence-coloring form: graphs avoiding any fixed subgraph F need O_F(Delta/logDelta) colors when their maximum degree Δ is sufficiently large. Also proves the Ajtai–Erdős–Komlós–Szemerédi independence conjecture: for fixed r ≥ 4, every n-vertex Kr-free graph of average degree d ≥ 2 has an independent set of size Omega_r(nlog d/d).

manuscripts.title: A logarithmic independence bound for clique-free graphs
Correspondence coloring graphs with a forbidden clique

families.title: Counterexamples to infinite matroid intersection and packing/covering
families.upstream_summary: Disproves the unrestricted infinite matroid intersection and packing/covering conjectures in ZFC, using two self-dual partitional matroids on a countably infinite ground set. The same examples answer Joó’s partitional-matroid question negatively. They are neither finitary nor cofinitary, so Nash-Williams’ original finitary conjecture remains outside the result.

manuscripts.title: A Counterexample to the Infinite Matroid Packing/Covering Conjecture

families.title: Uniform influence and sharp thresholds for graph and hypergraph properties
families.upstream_summary: Proves the Friedgut–Kalai threshold-width conjectures for graphs and fixed-uniformity hypergraphs. For fixed 0 < ε < 1/2, every nontrivial increasing relabeling-invariant property crosses from probability ε to 1-ε within width O((log n)^-2) for graphs and O_r((log n)^-r/(r-1)) for r-uniform hypergraphs, r ≥ 3. The hypergraph influence bound also applies to nonmonotone properties.

manuscripts.title: A Sharp Threshold Bound for Monotone Graph Properties
A uniform influence bound for hypergraph properties

families.title: Snaky in 21 Maker moves
families.upstream_summary: Settles the Snaky achievement problem: Maker can force the six-cell Snaky shape within 21 of its own moves on the initially empty infinite square board. Maker moves first, each player claims one free cell per turn, and translations, rotations and reflections count as wins.

manuscripts.title: Snaky in 21 Maker moves

families.title: The sharp terminal leave in random triangle removal
families.upstream_summary: Starting from the complete graph on n vertices, repeatedly delete a uniformly chosen remaining triangle. families.title: Boolean functions violate the square-root degree bound by arbitrary factors

families.title: The Kadison–Ringrose cohomology conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Proves that every bounded Hochschild cocycle of degree at least two on a complex von Neumann algebra, with coefficients in the algebra itself, has a bounded primitive. Equivalently, all higher bounded Hochschild cohomology groups vanish, resolving the Kadison–Ringrose conjecture.

manuscripts.title: Vanishing of higher bounded Hochschild cohomology

families.title: The generator problem for finite factors
families.upstream_summary: Proves that every type II₁ factor with separable predual is generated by a single operator, equivalently by two self-adjoint operators, resolving the generator problem. More strongly, for every irreducible inclusion Psubset M of such factors, the unitaries u with M=W^*(P,u) form a dense Gδ subset in the trace 2-norm topology.

manuscripts.title: Relative generation and the generator problem for finite factors

families.title: A ZFC counterexample to Naimark's problem
families.upstream_summary: Gives an alternative to [Tanaka's ZFC construction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26930v1) of a unital infinite-dimensional simple complex C∗-algebra with a faithful tracial state and exactly one nonzero irreducible representation up to unitary equivalence. Thus the unrestricted compact-operator characterization fails without additional set-theoretic assumptions; the counterexample is nonseparable.

manuscripts.title: A counterexample to Naimark's problem in ZFC

families.title: Two notions of free entropy differ even when both are finite
families.upstream_summary: Constructs a bounded self-adjoint tuple in a tracial von Neumann algebra whose microstates and nonmicrostates free entropies satisfy -∞ < chi < chi^* < ∞. This answers Voiculescu’s finite-entropy equality question negatively: the matrix-approximation and free-Fisher-information definitions differ even when both are finite.

manuscripts.title: A finite-entropy separation of microstates and nonmicrostates free entropy

families.title: The Kirchberg–Rørdam character criterion and infinite tensor-power Jiang–Su stability
families.upstream_summary: A nonzero unital separable complex C∗-algebra is Jiang–Su stable exactly when its norm central-sequence algebra has no characters, for every free ultrafilter. This answers the Kirchberg–Rørdam character question. Also, the infinite minimal tensor power of every such algebra without characters is Jiang–Su stable, answering the Dadarlat–Toms question.

manuscripts.title: The Kirchberg–Rørdam character criterion

families.title: Approximation and quadratic strong-operator paving
families.upstream_summary: Proves that every self-adjoint element of a complex von Neumann algebra admits strong-operator paving relative to any maximal abelian subalgebra with O(ε^-2) blocks. The norm bound holds after compression by a projection arbitrarily close to the identity in the strong topology, resolving the Popa–Vaes quadratic paving conjecture.

manuscripts.title: Approximation Paving over Arbitrary Maximal Abelian Subalgebras

families.title: Trace cones and Razak–Jacelon stabilization
families.upstream_summary: Classifies separable nuclear complex C∗-algebras after tensoring with the Razak–Jacelon algebra and the compact operators, using their full topological cones of extended lower-semicontinuous tracial weights. This answers Robert’s trace-cone question, including algebras with arbitrary ideal structure and both finite and infinite subquotients.

manuscripts.title: The trace cone classifies Razak–Jacelon stabilizations

families.title: Radius of comparison equals half the mean dimension
families.upstream_summary: For every minimal homeomorphism h of an infinite compact metrizable space X, the radius of comparison of C(X)rtimes_hℤ equals tfrac12mdim(X,h), including infinite values. Zero mean dimension is equivalent to the small boundary property, Jiang–Su stability and finite nuclear dimension; in this case nuclear dimension is at most one.

manuscripts.title: Filtered products and boundary-preserving compression in complex cobordism
Radius of comparison equals half the mean dimension

families.title: Weak pure infiniteness and Cuntz-algebra absorption
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the ordinary-to-strong pure-infiniteness question of Kirchberg and Rørdam for complex C∗-algebras. For exact algebras, proper infiniteness of one fixed finite amplification of every positive element also suffices. Consequently, every separable nuclear algebra with this property absorbs O_∞, without unitality or simplicity assumptions.

manuscripts.title: Weak pure infiniteness and O-infinity absorption

families.title: The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every dimension
families.upstream_summary: Every locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold is a Lie group. This proves the Hilbert–Smith conjecture in all finite dimensions, for Hausdorff second-countable manifolds without boundary.

manuscripts.title: The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every finite dimension

families.title: Four-dimensional disk embedding and Wall's conjecture
families.upstream_summary: The unrestricted four-dimensional disk-embedding conjecture fails: framed algebraic dual spheres do not suffice to obtain disjoint locally flat spanning disks. In particular, the free group F₂ is not good in the sense of Freedman–Quinn. Also constructs a finitely presented integral Poincaré duality group of dimension four with a finite classifying space but no realization as the fundamental group of a closed aspherical topological four-manifold, disproving Wall's conjecture.

A marked tensor obstruction to four-dimensional disk embedding

families.title: The purely cosmetic surgery conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Distinct Dehn surgery slopes on a nontrivial smooth knot in S³ never produce orientation-preservingly homeomorphic manifolds, proving the purely cosmetic surgery conjecture. The statement includes the meridional slope.

manuscripts.title: Purely cosmetic surgery on knots in the three-sphere

families.title: Failure of rational injectivity for maximal coarse assembly
families.upstream_summary: Constructs a uniformly discrete bounded-geometry space whose maximal coarse assembly map is not rationally injective. The example is a coarse disjoint union of finite connected graphs of uniformly bounded degree, with an infinite-order kernel class. families.title: Finite Smith–Toda complexes at every height
families.upstream_summary: For every n ≥ 0, constructs a finite Smith–Toda spectrum at a prime p depending on n, with Brown–Peterson homology BP_*/(p,v_1,ldots,v_n) and the canonical comodule structure. Thus Smith–Toda complexes exist at every height when the prime may vary; an explicit example realizes V(4) at p = 1009.

manuscripts.title: A finite Smith–Toda complex V(4) at the prime 1009
Finite Smith–Toda Complexes at Varying Primes

families.title: The Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the odd-primary Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three: exactly the standard classes with indices 0, 2, and 3 survive in the mod-three Adams spectral sequence, in stems 10, 106, and 322. Each surviving detection coset contains an element of exact additive order three.

manuscripts.title: The Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three

families.title: Quillen's conjecture in rational homology
families.upstream_summary: Proves the rational-homology form of Quillen's conjecture for every finite group and every prime. If the largest normal p-subgroup of G is trivial, the poset of nontrivial elementary abelian p-subgroups has nonzero augmented reduced rational homology and is therefore not contractible.

manuscripts.title: Rational homology and Quillen's conjecture

families.title: The Hovey–Strickland and Chai conjectures
families.upstream_summary: Proves Chai's invariant-ideal conjecture for Lubin–Tate deformation rings over finite residue fields, at every prime and positive height n. Through the implication of Barthel–Heard–Naumann, this proves the Hovey–Strickland conjecture: dualizable K(n)-local spectra have exactly n+2 thick tensor ideals, and their Balmer spectrum is a chain of n+1 points.

manuscripts.title: Stabilizer orbits and thick tensor ideals of dualizable K(n)-local spectra

families.title: The Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis
families.upstream_summary: Proves the Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis for ∞-groupoids associated with every Grothendieck coherator in the Ara–Henry convention: these algebraic objects recover the homotopy theory of spaces.

manuscripts.title: The Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis via elementary expansions

families.title: Finite generation for the K(n)-local sphere
families.upstream_summary: Answers the degreewise finiteness question of Hovey and Hovey–Strickland: every homotopy group of the K(n)-local sphere is a finitely generated ℤp-module, for every prime, positive height and integer degree. The same conclusion holds after K(n)-localizing any finite p-local spectrum.

manuscripts.title: Finite generation for the K(n)-local sphere

families.title: Cyclic length and chromatic fixed-point loss
families.upstream_summary: Determines the optimal chromatic loss from geometric H-fixed points to geometric G-fixed points for every subgroup H of a finite p-group G. At every nonnegative height, the loss equals the shortest subnormal-chain length from H to G with cyclic quotients. Each quotient counts once regardless of order, and finite spectra witness sharpness.

manuscripts.title: Cyclic length and chromatic fixed-point loss

families.title: The four-dimensional Singer conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Proves that the L²-Betti numbers of the universal cover of every closed connected aspherical topological four-manifold vanish outside degree two. More generally, the same conclusion holds for every finite connected aspherical integral Poincaré complex of formal dimension four, proving the four-dimensional Singer conjecture in this wider class.

manuscripts.title: The Singer conjecture in dimension four

families.title: Curtis’s conjecture
families.upstream_summary: Proves Curtis’s conjecture: the positive-degree mod-two stable Hurewicz image of the sphere is spanned by the images of the Hopf-invariant-one classes η, ν, σ and the Kervaire-invariant-one classes that exist.

families.title: Thomason model structures in all strict higher dimensions

families.title: Counterexamples to finite generation at chromatic height two
families.upstream_summary: Refutes the Hahn–Wilson conjecture at chromatic height two. For every sufficiently large prime p, constructs a connective p-complete spectrum of exact fp-type two that cannot be built from completed BPlangle2rangle by finitely many sums, shifts, cones and retracts. manuscripts.title: Counterexamples to the Hahn-Wilson conjecture at height two

families.title: Nonhomeomorphic closed aspherical four-manifolds
families.upstream_summary: Constructs closed connected aspherical topological four-manifolds that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic, with a common word-hyperbolic fundamental group. This disproves even the homeomorphism-existence formulation of the Borel conjecture in dimension four.

families.title: A counterexample to Wall's finite D(2) problem
families.upstream_summary: Constructs a finite connected three-dimensional CW complex whose universal cover has no integral homology above degree two and whose third cohomology vanishes for every local coefficient module, but which has no finite two-dimensional homotopy model.
