families.title: Tingley’s sphere-isometry problem
families.upstream_summary: Resolves Tingley's problem: every surjective isometry between the unit spheres of nonzero real Banach spaces extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry of the whole spaces. No dimension restriction is imposed, so the metric geometry of the unit sphere determines the Banach space up to linear isometry.

families.title: Independence of the separable quotient problem

families.title: The complete Crouzeix conjecture

families.title: Markov type characterizes superreflexivity

families.title: Nonexpansive fixed points in reflexive Banach spaces

manuscripts.title: Fixed Points of Nonexpansive Maps in Reflexive Banach Spaces

families.title: A counterexample to metric-entropy duality
families.upstream_summary: Disproves Pietsch's dimension-free duality conjecture for metric entropy. Origin-symmetric convex bodies violate every proposed choice of universal constants in the conjectured comparison between covering numbers and those of the polar bodies, even when the covering body is a cube.

families.title: A uniformly discrete counterexample to bounded approximation in Lipschitz-free spaces
families.upstream_summary: Constructs a countable uniformly discrete metric space whose real Lipschitz-free Banach space has the approximation property but not the bounded approximation property, answering Kalton's question negatively. families.title: Metric Markov cotype of ℓ₁ and Hilbert-space Lipschitz extension
families.upstream_summary: Proves that real ℓ₁ has metric Markov cotype two, answering Mendel and Naor's question. families.title: Smooth isometric immersions of surfaces into ℝ⁴

families.title: A smooth surface metric with no local isometric immersion in ℝ³

families.title: Yau's uniformization conjecture

families.title: Weak MTW curvature gives convexity and regular optimal transport
families.upstream_summary: On every closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension at least two satisfying weak Ma–Trudinger–Wang curvature, all tangent injectivity domains are convex, resolving Villani’s conjecture in this setting. For squared-distance transport between measurable probability densities bounded above and away from zero, the optimal map and its inverse are Hölder continuous.

manuscripts.title: Global Support and Convex Injectivity Domains under Weak MTW
Uniform Bi-Holder Transport from Weak MTW

families.title: Failure of integer-degree harmonic dimension comparison
families.upstream_summary: Disproves Yau's proposed Euclidean dimension bound for harmonic functions of integer growth on manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature. For every sufficiently large integer k, a complete smooth metric on ℝ³ has at least (k+2)^2 independent harmonic functions of growth at most k, exceeding the Euclidean count (k+1)^2. The metric may depend on k.

manuscripts.title: A counterexample to integer-degree harmonic dimension comparison
A Three-Dimensional Counterexample to Integer-Degree Harmonic Dimension Comparison

families.title: Global smoothness for relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell
families.upstream_summary: Proves large-data global existence and uniqueness for the three-dimensional, one-species relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system. Smooth admissible initial data may be arbitrary provided the particle density is compactly supported and the electromagnetic fields have finite energy and bounded derivatives of every order; the solution remains smooth on every finite time interval.

manuscripts.title: Global classical solutions of the three-dimensional relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system

lenses.why: The family treats large-data global smoothness for the relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system.

families.title: Nonuniqueness with local conservation for the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation
families.upstream_summary: Constructs two distinct global entropy solutions of the three-dimensional periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation from the same nonnegative initial density, with bounded velocity support and finite mass, energy and absolute entropy. Both are strongly continuous in L¹ and satisfy exact local conservation of mass, momentum and kinetic energy.

manuscripts.title: Nonuniqueness for the periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation
Nonuniqueness with local conservation for the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation

lenses.why: The family treats nonuniqueness for entropy solutions of the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation.

families.title: Kinetic limits and fluctuations over the Boltzmann lifespan
families.upstream_summary: Derives the nonlinear Boltzmann equation from three-dimensional grand-canonical Newtonian gases throughout every regular kinetic interval with uniform Gaussian decay. Stable finite-range radial potentials may have attractive wells and a singular repulsive core; initial pair exclusion and spatially summable Gaussian density and gradient bounds are assumed. A companion gives finite-dimensional hard-sphere Gaussian fluctuations, centered at the exact microscopic expectation and governed by the linear fluctuating Boltzmann equation.

manuscripts.title: Hard-sphere fluctuations on the regular Boltzmann lifespan
The Boltzmann–Grad limit for stable radial potentials on regular kinetic intervals

lenses.why: The family treats kinetic limits from Newtonian particle systems to the Boltzmann equation.

families.title: Joint metric and connection recovery from one boundary patch
families.upstream_summary: Zero-frequency measurements on any nonempty open boundary patch determine a smooth metric and smooth unitary connection on a trivial Hermitian rank-two bundle over a compact connected manifold of dimension at least three, up to diffeomorphism and gauge fixed on that patch. Inputs and observations use the same patch. In contrast, distinct uniformly positive bounded measurable scalar conductivities on a three-dimensional ball can have identical full-boundary data.

manuscripts.title: Nonuniqueness for bounded measurable scalar conductivities in three dimensions
Smooth anisotropic uniqueness in the Calderón problem from one boundary patch
Determination of a metric and a unitary connection from one boundary patch

families.title: The planar Mumford–Shah regularity conjecture and local weak-L⁴ gradient bounds
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the interior regularity conjecture for reduced absolute planar Mumford–Shah minimizers with bounded fidelity data. Locally, the closed discontinuity set is a C^1,α arc, a regular crack tip, or three arcs meeting at 120^circ; only finitely many global connected components meet any compact interior region.

manuscripts.title: Interior regularity of planar Mumford–Shah minimizers

families.title: The critical dimension for the one-phase Bernoulli problem
families.upstream_summary: Establishes seven as the first dimension admitting a nonflat, one-homogeneous global minimizer of the one-phase Bernoulli energy. Consequently, minimizing free boundaries are smooth through dimension six, and their singular sets have dimension at most n-7 in higher dimensions.

manuscripts.title: The critical dimension for one-phase Bernoulli minimizers

families.title: The three-dimensional Ball–Evans approximation problem
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the three-dimensional Ball–Evans approximation problem: every W^1,p homeomorphism between arbitrary bounded domains in ℝ³, for 1 ≤ p < ∞, is a strong W^1,p limit of smooth diffeomorphisms onto the same target.

manuscripts.title: Strong diffeomorphic approximation in three dimensions for 1≤p≤2
Strong diffeomorphic approximation in three dimensions for p>2

families.title: The hot spots conjecture for simply connected planar domains
families.upstream_summary: Proves a strict form of Burdzy's simply connected hot spots conjecture. On every smooth bounded simply connected planar domain, each nonzero eigenfunction for the first positive Neumann eigenvalue has no interior critical point, so all global extrema lie on the boundary. Eigenvalue multiplicity is allowed.

manuscripts.title: Strict hot spots and absence of interior critical points on smooth simply connected planar domains

families.title: The Lane–Emden and Hénon–Lane–Emden conjectures
families.upstream_summary: Resolves the subcritical Lane–Emden conjecture and its weighted Hénon extension. For n ≥ 2, p,q > 0 and real A, B, the system -Delta u=|x|^A v^p, -Delta v=|x|^B u^q has no positive entire solution when (n+A)/(p+1)+(n+B)/(q+1) > n-2, with solutions continuous at the origin and classical elsewhere. No symmetry or growth assumption is needed. Known radial existence gives the exact existence criterion for n ≥ 3 and A,B > -2.

manuscripts.title: The Subcritical Hénon–Lane–Emden Conjecture

families.title: Stable blowup for the defocusing Schrödinger equation
families.upstream_summary: For a sufficiently large odd nonlinearity power, constructs a nonempty open set of initial data in H^k(T^12), with k > 8, whose solutions of the scalar defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation blow up in finite time. Thus finite-time blowup is stable under Sobolev perturbations in this supercritical regime.

manuscripts.title: Stable self-similar blowup for a supercritical defocusing Schrödinger equation on the torus

families.title: Global uniqueness in smooth isotropic elasticity
families.upstream_summary: Proves that full static boundary displacement-to-traction data determine both smooth real Lamé moduli on every bounded connected smooth domain in ℝ³, provided μ > 0 and 3λ+2μ > 0 on the closure. Neither analyticity, proximity to constant coefficients nor prior knowledge near the boundary is required.

manuscripts.title: Global Uniqueness for the Smooth Isotropic Elasticity Inverse Problem

families.title: Nonattainment of the three-marginal Coulomb Monge problem
families.upstream_summary: An optimal three-particle Coulomb configuration need not be a deterministic function of the first particle, even for smooth identical spatial densities. The Monge and Kantorovich infima agree, but the Monge infimum is not attained. The same phenomenon occurs for every inverse-power Riesz exponent in each dimension at least two, with a suitable density in each case.

manuscripts.title: A counterexample to the Monge ansatz for the three-marginal Coulomb cost

lenses.why: The family treats nonattainment for a three-marginal Coulomb transport problem.

families.title: Sharp one-third stability of Brenier maps
families.upstream_summary: For uniform source measure ρ on a compact convex body with interior in dimension at least two, quadratic optimal transport maps satisfy ‖T_μ-T_ν‖_L^2(ρ) ≤ C W_2(μ,ν)^1/3 uniformly over targets in a fixed compact set. The exponent is sharp, even for three-atom targets, disproving Letrouit's conjectured square-root bound.

manuscripts.title: Sharp One-Third Stability of Brenier Maps

families.title: De Giorgi's conjecture in dimension eight
families.upstream_summary: Proves De Giorgi's conjecture at its sharp dimension-eight endpoint: every entire C² solution u:ℝ^8 → (-1,1) of Delta u=u^3-u that is strictly increasing in one direction depends on only one linear coordinate. A stronger theorem classifies all stable entire solutions v:ℝ^7 → [-1,1] as constant wells or planar transitions, without an energy-growth assumption.

manuscripts.title: A positive resolution of De Giorgi's conjecture in dimension eight

lenses.why: The family treats one-dimensional symmetry for phase-interface solutions of the Allen–Cahn equation in dimension eight.

families.title: Universal computation in forced Navier–Stokes flows
families.upstream_summary: Constructs viscous incompressible flows starting from rest on a fixed flat three-dimensional domain that perform universal computation under smooth external forcing. A terminating compiler turns a Turing machine and input into a finite program for the force, so a designated particle reaches a fixed region exactly when the machine halts. The viscosity is fixed, positive and computable.

families.title: Interior C^1,α regularity for infinity-harmonic functions
families.upstream_summary: Proves uniform interior C^1,α_d regularity for bounded infinity-harmonic functions in every dimension d ≥ 3, for a positive exponent depending only on dimension. The gradient's supremum norm and Hölder seminorm on the half unit ball are bounded by a dimension-dependent constant times the oscillation on the unit ball. The exponent is not explicit.

paper.title: Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search
paper.abstract_claim: Our most capable agent autonomously resolved 9 of 353 open Erdős problems at the per-problem cost of a few hundred dollars, proved 44/492 OEIS conjectures, and is being deployed in combinatorics, optimization, graph theory, algebraic geometry, and quantum optics research.
paper.table1_caption: Open problems from the ErdosProblems repository autonomously resolved by our full-featured agent. The asterisk indicates a variant of the main problem with this number. Problem #26 (annotated with †) is a more general variant of a question posed by Erdős, but was not posed by Erdős himself.
paper.density_note: For example, in Erdős problems #125 and #741(i), the interpretation of “density” in the original informal statements was amended to “lower density” and “upper density” respectively, after our full-featured agent found proofs using density as “natural density.” Following the correction of the ambiguity, the agent was still able to resolve the questions.
paper.agent_a: To understand the impact of the agent design on these results, we did a post-hoc analysis of the performance of the full-featured and basic agents, as well as two agents with intermediate capabilities, on the 9 Erdős problems solved by the full-featured agent. Remarkably, the basic agent solved all 9 problems, though at a higher cost on the harder problems.

quotations: Our most capable agent autonomously resolved 9 of 353 open Erdős problems at the per-problem cost of a few hundred dollars, proved 44/492 OEIS conjectures, and is being deployed in combinatorics, optimization, graph theory, algebraic geometry, and quantum optics research.

Open problems from the ErdosProblems repository autonomously resolved by our full-featured agent. The asterisk indicates a variant of the main problem with this number. Problem #26 (annotated with †) is a more general variant of a question posed by Erdős, but was not posed by Erdős himself.

For example, in Erdős problems #125 and #741(i), the interpretation of “density” in the original informal statements was amended to “lower density” and “upper density” respectively, after our full-featured agent found proofs using density as “natural density.” Following the correction of the ambiguity, the agent was still able to resolve the questions.

To understand the impact of the agent design on these results, we did a post-hoc analysis of the performance of the full-featured and basic agents, as well as two agents with intermediate capabilities, on the 9 Erdős problems solved by the full-featured agent. Remarkably, the basic agent solved all 9 problems, though at a higher cost on the harder problems.
